title: Evenflow deploy memo — evening release cadence notes
content:
Quick context and intent:
- Purpose: capture a lightweight, repeatable evening deployment pattern I can run solo (or hand to on-call) when we need a low-friction canary that minimizes oscillation and unnecessary rollbacks.
- Why "evenflow": aim to smooth traffic ramp-up/decay so we avoid sudden load spikes, reduce client jitter, and keep metric noise low for decision windows. Think of it as a thermostat with small, bounded adjustments, not hard flips.

High-level plan (one-liner):
- 00:00: stabilize baseline checks -> 00:05: start 0.5% probe -> 00:20: quiet ramp to 3% if all green -> 00:50: open to 15% steady growth (with step holds and drift checks) -> decision at 2h.

Quick preflight checklist (pre-run, target = evening window):
- ✅ Verify infra health dashboard (node counts, GPU readiness, scheduler queue < 5%)
- ✅ Check last 24h error rates and latency 95/99 for each affected route (note baseline numbers)
- ✅ Confirm model artifacts: version tag, hash, diff summary from previous release
- ✅ Confirm fallback policy present (auto-fallback to last-good model variant) and feature gate path
- ✅ Notify #releases and on-call via short message with expected timeline and rollback triggers

Probe & ramp recipe (detailed steps):
1) Probe (0–10 minutes)
  - Start at 0.5% of traffic (cohort sampling seed to deterministic client ids).
  - Hold for 15 minutes (observability window).
  - Watchlist: 5xx rate, client tail latency (99th), token generation tail, queue time, OOMs.
  - Acceptance: no >50% relative regression on 5xx and tail latency within +25ms over baseline, no new spike in memory or OOM.
2) Gentle ramp (10–60 minutes)
  - If probe OK: step to 3% and hold 20 minutes.
  - If still OK: step to 8% and hold 20 minutes.
  - At each hold: run a small set of synthetic prompts (known prompts from regression suite) against both cohorts and diff outputs for hallucination or truncation.
3) Broad ramp (60–120 minutes)
  - Move to 15% if cumulative signals good.
  - After 2 hours, evaluate readiness for 50% or full release depending on product team signoff.

Safety thresholds (hard triggers for immediate rollback):
- Any sustained 5xx > 0.5% absolute or >5x baseline for 5 continuous minutes.
- 99th latency increase >200ms over baseline for >10 minutes.
- Error patterns that correlate with specific customers (tenant blackout).
- Memory/Disk/Peers OOMs in the serving pool.
- Significant degradations in quality checks: core prompt recall falls >3 F1 points or hallucination rate > baseline + 4%.

Soft alerts (investigate, consider pinback or partial rollback):
- Minor upticks in client-reported errors (support tickets with matching timestamps).
- Slight drift in token efficiency (costs per 1k tokens > 10% uplift).
- Model output scoring drop on small eval set (single-output issues) — might be reversible by prompt tweak.

Observability & instrumentation notes (what I look at live):
- Infra: node pod restarts, scheduler backlog, GPU util, queue depth.
- App: request latencies P50/P95/P99, request duration histogram, token production rate, CPU steal/GC events.
- SLOs/Errors: 5xx rate, per-route error breakdown, per-tenant error heatmap.
- Quality: small streaming harness that runs 20 golden prompts every 10 minutes; store diffs and alert on outliers.

Operational scripts / quick commands (personal handy list):
- Rollback to stable tag: ./deploy --pin stable-2026-02-10 --force-restart
- Shrink cohort to 0.1%: ./traffic-sculpt --set 0.1 --cohort evenflow-probe
- Dump failing requests (when investigating): curl admin/trace?since=2026-03-10T20:00Z
- Quick health scrape: ./healthcheck --routes my-service --json | jq '.'

Post-deploy checks and notes (first 2 hours):
- Record the minute-by-minute 5xx and latency deltas into the release spreadsheet (link in linked_artifacts).
- Capture top 3 anomalous traces and paste into the incident thread if present.
- Leave a short status update in #releases at 30m, 60m, 120m.

Open questions to resolve next run (TODOs):
- Should we bias cohort sampling to lower-risk tenants for initial probe? Pros/cons for product.
- Evaluate automated small prompt-set A/B evaluation for difference fuzz vs human review cadence.
- Add a micro-canary path that automatically reduces token limit if latency spikes (rate-limited mitigation).

Notes to self / heuristics learned (informal):
- Evening runs: lower background traffic makes small anomalies more visible — avoid overreacting to single outliers unless repeated.
- Small step sizes are better than large leaps; client SDKs sometimes amplify small latency changes via retries.
- Always have an escape hatch that pins to previous artefact rather than immediate global rollback (fastest to reestablish baseline).

If you run this template: copy the checklist, paste times into a calendar event, ping on-call, and try to keep the first hold windows long enough to capture tail behaviour (I prefer 15–20m).

End of memo.

Unresolved / scribbles:
- Consider a 'quiet-swap' API that pulls traffic from cohorts with minimal telemetry noise and logs only the delta.
- Might automate the synthetic prompt harness to run as a sidecar in canary instances (avoid cross-traffic contamination).

-- noah
